recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core. Future Permission resource work should occur in HL7/data-access-policies unless a later final work group decision moves Permission back into the active FHIR core build.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive Security issue, applied for R5, requesting creation of a Permission resource for requirements, presumed permissions, and acquired permissions to use data in contexts not covered by Consent, including non-patient policy or contract based access-control cases.
initial_application: Commit 3e3089515a27ab6af3c234f23bb4ec6596878ee2 was tagged J#25933 and added source/permission, fhir.ini entries, status codes, hierarchy/resource-list entries, examples, and Permission narrative/notes. Later commits including 413b45eb634006984af72b514b616aab2f1a9808 refined the model and examples in line with Jira comments, and 6c38b08bca9b9e42cb050da731e31de3d7ba95c8 marked Permission approved.
additional_context: Current core no longer owns Permission source. Commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 removed source/permission, the active Permission entries in source/fhir.ini, related status-code rows, core hierarchy/resource-list references, and Consent.provisionReference, while redirecting Security/history references to the Data Access Policies IG. Security WG minutes on 2025-08-25 record a 9-0-0 motion to keep Permission out of FHIR R6 core as a non-core resource to enable its evolution.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No core source file was changed because reintroducing the R5 source/permission resource or active fhir.ini entries would conflict with the later current-build ownership decision.
